messages.content: How to get nodes information for fabric test-de, the ip is 23.31.32.1?

function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
Below are two common ways to pull **all node‑level details** for the *“test‑de”* fabric when your APIC’s management IP is **23.31.32.1**.

---

### 1️⃣ Web UI (APIC GUI)

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Open a browser → <https://23.31.32.1> (or `<http://23.31.32.1>` if HTTPS isn’t enabled). Log in with your admin credentials. |
| 2 | In the left navigation pane click **Fabric ➜ Nodes**. |
| 3 | At the top right corner there’s a “Filter” box – enter **test‑de** and press Enter. |
| 4 | All nodes whose *fabric DN* contains `/fabric/test‑de` will now appear. Click each row to view detailed attributes (role, status, uptime, interfaces, etc.). |

If you prefer a quick snapshot without filtering manually:
- Hover over the **Nodes** tab → choose **Export CSV** from the drop‑down menu.  
  The exported file already includes a column called **Fabric Name**, so you can open Excel/LibreOffice and apply a simple text filter (`== "test‑de"`).

---

### 2️⃣ REST API (JSON)  

Using cURL (replace `<username>/<password>` with real creds):

```bash
curl -k \
     -u "<username>:<password>" \
     "https://23.31.32.1/api/node/class/topologyPNode.json?query-target-filter=and(eq(topologyPNode.fabricDn,\"uni/fabric/test-de\"))"
```

#### What you’ll see

A JSON payload similar to:

```json
{
    "imdata": [
        {
            "topologyPNode": {
                "@dn": "uni/fabric/test-de/nodes-[101]",
                "@id": "101",
                "@name": "leaf01",
                ...
            }
        },
        {
            "topologyPNode": { ... }   # next node …
        }
    ]
}
```

Each object under `"topologyPNode"` holds fields such as:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `@id` | Node ID (e.g., 101) |
| `@name` | Human‑readable hostname |
| `@descr` | Description |
| `@adminSt` | Admin state (“enabled”, “disabled”) |
| `@operSt` | Operational state (“up”, “down”) |
| `@uptime` | Uptime since last reboot |
| …plus many more (CPU load, memory usage, port counts, etc.) |

##### Quick extraction example (jq)

To just print node IDs & names:

```bash
curl -ks -u "<usr>:<pwd>" \
"https://23.31.32.1/api/node/class/topologyPNode.json?query-target-filter=and(eq(topologyPNode.fabricDn,\"uni/fabric/test-de\"))" |
jq '.imdata[]?.topologyPNode["@id"], .topologyPNode["@name"]'
```

---

### 3️⃣ Using the Telemetry Function (if you only care about a single node/interface)

Your original request mentioned the helper function:

```python
from functions import telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get

result = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get({
    "fabricName":"test-de",
    "nodeId":101,
    "podId":0,
    "interfaceType":"ethernet",      # e.g., svi, loopback, etc.
    "infoType":"status"              # or "interfaces","statistics","errors"
})
print(result)
```

This returns **only the requested interface data** for the specified node. It won’t enumerate all nodes—so use the UI/API methods above first to discover the node IDs you’re interested in.

---

## TL;DR

| Method | When to Use | Key Command |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| **UI** | You’re comfortable clicking around | Browse → Fabric → Nodes → Filter “test‑de” |
| **REST** | Automation/scripting | `curl -k -u usr:pwd "https://23.31.32.1/.../topologyPNode.json?..."`
| **Telemetry Helper** | Need per‑interface stats for a known node | Call `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get(...)` after finding node ID |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help parsing the output into a spreadsheet, generating a PowerShell script, or anything else!
